review_notes: Ordinary attribute assignment maps to dictionary keys, while names already defined on the class or inherited dictionary methods remain read-only. The mutation inverts this object-protocol boundary; preserve the library existing AttributeError contract and nested mapping ownership. Source Smith patch introduces the defect. Original required lists/full-file scope preserved; baseline diagnostic error is expected reproduction, not a policy failure.

arguments.command:
python3 - <<'PYREPLAY'
from pathlib import Path
import hashlib, importlib, sys, pytest
module=importlib.import_module('addict.addict')
actual=Path(module.__file__).resolve()
expected=(Path.cwd()/'addict/addict.py').resolve()
assert actual==expected,(actual,expected)
print('source_binding',actual,'sha256',hashlib.sha256(actual.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),'Python',sys.version.split()[0],'pytest',pytest.__version__)
from addict import Dict
d=Dict()
try:
 d.color=7
 normal=('color' in d and d['color']==7 and d.color==7)
except Exception as exc:
 normal=type(exc).__name__,str(exc)
try:
 d.keys='blocked'
 protected=False
except AttributeError:
 protected=True
print('ordinary_attribute_to_key',normal,'class_method_protected',protected,'mapping',dict(d))
assert normal is True and protected is True and 'keys' not in d
class Child(Dict):
 @property
 def marker(self):return 'class-property'
c=Child()
c.answer=11
assert c['answer']==11 and c.answer==11
try:
 c.marker=12
 raise AssertionError('class property was overwritten')
except AttributeError:
 pass
c.nested.value=13
assert c['nested']['value']==13
print('attribute_mapping_and_class_namespace_contract',True)
PYREPLAY
